title: lib modules are committed in three copies
what: Each lib module exists once in the repo; the plugins load it from that one place (a path resolved from the plugin's own location, or the plugin build copies it outside git), and bin/sync-lib-copies goes away.
why: Owner, 26 Oct: "агенты позволяют нам делать множество изменений одновременно, большие файлы - наши враги, концентрируя большой объем кода (смысла) они являются поводом для конфликтов", then "a" (principle 10 "one subject per file, no hub files, no copies" plus four items). Measured over 5 days: bin/relay (887 lines) in 44 commits, lib/relay_queue.py (1189 lines) in 25 commits kept in 3 copies, lib/relay_setup.py (1134 lines) changed by 3 open branches at once (license, setup-wt, the portable-tool design). IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen). Every change to relay_queue.py touches 3 files (25 commits x 3 in 5 days); principle 3, a built file committed beside its source.
failing_case: git ls-files | grep relay_queue.py lists 3 paths with identical content.
pass_cases: One path; the plugins' hooks and commands that used a copy still run (their tests pass); a session started with only the plugins folder still finds the module.

fact: 30 Oct, front decision (owner can reverse; principle 9, follows from principles 2 and 7): build the reviewed design reports/design-lib-one-copy.md now with relative symlinks for the 34 copied files under plugins/*/lib (31 .py, 3 prices.toml); estimated 55 agent minutes plus 35-40 to resolve the two open branches that touch copies, against about 30 agent minutes a day of fix-up commits if it waited (design estimates, not measured). Relay's folder as seen by shared code stays as today; its three wrong reads are a separate fix item. Windows out of scope.
